title: Free Trip to Historic Philadelphia
description:
Join the History Club for a full-day trip to Philadelphia as we explore some of the most historic places in the United States.
We’ll visit Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell, followed by stops at the Museum of the American Revolution and the National Constitution Center. Together, these sites tell the story of the nation’s founding. We'll learn about the debates and ideals that shaped the country and how those ideas have been interpreted, challenged, and expanded over time.
This trip is an opportunity to reflect on the past 250 years of American history while also thinking about the kind of country we hope to build in the next 250.
To wrap up the day, we’ll head to Dave and Buster’s to relax, grab dinner, and spend time together before returning home.
This trip is part of Montclair State University’s Montclair 250 celebrations.

Hosted by: The Historical Society at Montclair State

description:

title: Hike Like the Gorale - Polish Highlander Experience
description:
Join the Polish Club for an exciting outdoor adventure inspired by the Górale, the traditional highland people of southern Poland known for their love of nature, hiking, music, and strong cultural pride.
Participants will enjoy a group hike while learning about Góral traditions, clothing, folklore, and life in the Tatra Mountains. This event promotes wellness, cultural appreciation, and community building in a fun and active setting. Whether you are an experienced hiker or just looking for a scenic walk, everyone is welcome to participate.
Please wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. Come ready to explore, connect, and experience Polish culture in a unique way!

description:

location: Van Vleck House & Gardens, 21 Van Vleck Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Saturday, 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM 
April 11th – Arbor Day Everyday 
Arbor Day is a day to reflect on the importance of trees in our environment. We have an abundance of beautiful trees throughout the gardens. At April’s Outdoor Adventures, learn more about our trees as we explore their role in our environment, their unique leaf shapes, and what animals use trees as their homes.  
Join us in the gardens as you and your family explore and learn about the outdoor world through crafts, scavenger hunts, activity sheets and educational displays. Each program will focus on a specific theme, and our Van Vleck Education team will guide your family through this interactive learning experience. This program is entirely outdoors, weather dependent. Registration is required and includes everything you need to participate in the program. Designed for children ages 4 -11 but all are welcome. 
Fee: FREE for Members of Van Vleck; $15 per family  for  General Public 
Registration required by 1 day prior to each class 
 
Sponsored by  
  
Upcoming Outdoor Adventures: 
May 16th – Honeybees & Hummingbirds 
What do bees and hummingbirds have in common? They fly and they are pollinators! Join us to learn about your local pollinators, how they make a positive impact on our environment, and what we can do to help them on their mission.  
  
June 6th – Insect Safari  
You can find many different insects buzzing, wiggling, and crawling around the gardens. Join us for an Insect Safari at this month’s Outdoor Adventures. Create a bug inspired craft, take a hike looking for insects, and learn about the important roles insects play in the garden.

title: Daytime Pool at Clifton Billiards
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
***Trying something different this time, Saturday afternoon date and in the window for day passes! So if you are available and feel like staying longer, or coming closer to the middle or end, it's more flexible, easier to change between tables and play with more people and less time is spent counting hours, etc. We'll see how this pans out going forward.***

***Meeting Point:***
Outside of the building; After 5-10 minutes: You can meet us upstairs at the pool tables. *\*\*Please look for the group as the staff do not keep up with the group\*\***
*** Price:
Photo of the day passes pricing is posted, however if you only want to stay a short while and would rather pay less, the price is $6.50 per hour per person if you have 4 players at your table. However, the final price is based on the total amount of minutes played. At the end of the hour, the table amount will be split per person. Each table paying this way should have a table leader, **this person will collect the money of players at their table and will pay for the table on one card.** 3-4 table leaders will be needed, **volunteering for this is encouraged**

***Bringing cash is highly encouraged to pay your portion to your table leader***

*Parking*: street parking is available however it may be hard to find close to the venue. There are side streets before the town proper, but a good option is the nearby ANT bookstore which has a lot which should be okay to use.

***This location has food & drinks available for purchase.***

*** Expectations**:
Pool cues are available at the location, expect mid to low lighting. If you come after 7:15pm, look for the Meetup group upstairs.
** *What if I'm a beginner or only want to play with people at a similar level?**
Tables will be divided between beginners, intermediate players, and advanced. However, this depends on how many types of players come, so it will be divided as best as possibly available. If you would like game rules, please speak with Marc.** Marc is also available to answer questions including how to hold the cue, stances, etc.**
*** Is anyone at Clifton Billiards after the event is over?
Afterward, most go home or go to a local bar. If you'd like to hang out after, definitely speak with members to see if they want to do something after.
*** Can I switch tables?**
*Yes, but it does make it easier if you stay at your table. If you switch tables, pay the amount of time you were at that table. Example, if you were at able A for an hour, pay the hour to the table A leader. If you go table B for two hours, pay your two hours to the table B leader. At the end, the table leader is taking the payments for the total amount of time at that table.*
*** How do I get balls for the table and how many people do I tell staff that I have?*
*One person per table gives their ID to the staff in order to check out balls. Again, the price for 4 people is about $6.50. If you have more or less, it slightly changes. So it just depends on how many people are at your table. It may be better to mention that you have more people esp if you are starting with 4 or 5 people.*
*** I feel like people aren't trying to be my friend.*
*Please remember that different people have different goals. Some may come to just play billiards, others may be there to meet new people or do something social, and some may be there to make long term friends. Find people that match your goals or be ok with others that may not.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students
location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - April meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues/ (optional) "**Build Your Own ai Agent**" workshop ([more details here](https://www.meetup.com/nj-code-coffee/events/314048120))
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

* your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,
* What you can help others with,
* What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Building Your Own AI Agent: A Guided Walkthrough
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
As part of [April's monthly meetup](Building Your Own AI Agent: A Guided Walkthrough), NJ Code & Coffee presents "**Building Your Own AI Agent: A Guided Walkthrough**".

Join us for a guided walk through of the core principles of AI agents: completions, tools, and the agentic loop.

Whether you're AI-curious or already shipping with LLMs, you'll leave with a solid mental model of how agents actually work under the hood.

We'll use the Anthropic Claude API with the TypeScript SDK as our foundation, building up from a simple completion all the way to a fully autonomous agent.

Bring your laptop if you want to follow along; there'll be one hands-on moment where we build the agent loop together.

**All skill levels are welcome.**

**What You'll Learn:**

* How LLM completions actually work under the hood
* How to give agents tools and let them decide when to use them
* The agentic loop — how agents reason, act, and iterate autonomously
* How to build a working agent from scratch using the Anthropic TypeScript SDK
* Mental models for thinking about agents that you can apply to any framework

**What You’ll Need To Follow Along:**

* A laptop with the latest version of Node.js and git installed
* An Anthropic API key with a few dollars of credits loaded

**Doors open at 2pm, talk starts at 3, arrive early for networking and light refreshments.**
Bring your laptop.

**Speaker Bio:**

Aza Walker is a self-taught software engineer with a fascination for computers and the intricate systems that make them work.
He enjoys designing and building large-scale applications, and currently works at ShipBob as a Senior Software Engineer, where he focuses on developing scalable microservices.

description:
Get ready for a scenic spin through history as we ride the legendary Old Croton Aqueduct! This unforgettable bike trip takes you along one of New York’s most beautiful and peaceful trails, where tree-lined paths, and charming river views, create the perfect backdrop for a day outdoors. As we cruise along the trail you’ll enjoy plenty of photo-worthy stops along the way. Expect a relaxed pace with time to explore, snack, and soak in the scenery. title: Chester County Pastoral Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this excellent rural hike in Chester County PA, which ties together a different way the recent Chester County hikes we've been doing.
From the start, we will do the easier back roads.
The only lined road we will be on is the very beginning.
We will walk through the historic Sheeder-Hall Covered Bridge, then out to the main road for under a half mile, We then turn onto some back roads including Sheeder Mill Road, HIlltop Road, Birchrun Road, Green Lane, and Bartlett Road.
At least half of this is unpaved, and none of these named roads even have lines in them, making them narrow, lightly used, and very pleasant.
We'll soon get on the Horse-Shoe Trail from where we left off. This takes us through pleasant woods, and then out into cultivated farm fields.
Bits of the Horse-Shoe Trail also follow these little used roads.
We'll continue on the HST to Art School Lane, then make our way east and pass the historic Vincent Baptist Church and cemetery.
We'll continue to the intersection with Miller Road, where we'll begin following the Bryn Coed Trail System.
This amazing and long trail system weaves though woods and fields keeping with the overall theme of the hike.
Amazing pastoral views will make for a relaxing walk that will lead us almost all the way back to our stating point.
We'll get on one more dirt road before the end, and then an abandoned road that is now in the trail system right back to where we parked.
Distance 15 mi
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK** will begin this year with finishing work on the Lenape Trail reroute below the Beech Brook Cascades. The steps are in (see photo), but final tread improvements on switchbacks and throughout are needed. We will meet at the Dog Park (11 Bear Lane) and head down to the Lenape trail from there.

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants should wear long pants due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.)

title: Rug Tufting Workshop
location: The Eclectic Chic Boutique, 547 Bloomfield Avenue, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Learn how to make your own custom rug! This rug tufting class will guide you through creating your own custom rug using a tufting gun. You’ll learn essential techniques for handling the tufting gun safely and effectively, focusing entirely on mastering the craft since your design and yarn colors will already be prepared on the tufting frame. Once tufting is complete, you’ll discover how to apply glue and backing to secure and protect your rug. The class finishes with the exciting step of trimming excess yarn, revealing the final texture and look of your handmade rug. This hands-on experience combines creativity with practical skills to help you craft a unique, personalized piece. 
Upon booking you will receive a link to choose your rug design for the class. 
This is a great opportunity to make a fun gift, to keep or to give. Invite your partner, friends, family, or coworkers for a fun and creative day out. 
Bring a mask if you are sensitive to yarn particles and chemical smells from glue.

Second Sunday Concert: Teatro Nuovo
location: Van Vleck House & Gardens, 21 Van Vleck Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
April 12, 2PM 
Led by conductor/musicologist Will Crutchfield, Teatro Nuovo – Italian for “new theater” – is a young organization devoted to cutting-edge interpretation of classic Italian opera.  Since its debut in 2018, Teatro Nuovo has presented thirteen operas by Rossini, Donizetti, Bellini, Verdi, Ricci, and Mayr, culminating in the modern premiere of Carolina Uccelli’s Anna di Resburgo, which made the New York Times list of the 20 best Classical events for 2024.  This year Teatro Nuovo will celebrate the bicentennial of Italian opera in America.

This concert will show how delving into forgotten traditions can animate the future of the art, as Will Crutchfield and young vocal stars will perform virtuoso thrillers and heart-melting lyrics from the golden age of Italian Bel Canto. Don’t miss this exciting opportunity to hear some of opera’s newest rising stars! 
Members received the registration link in mid-March. This concert is free but a donation of $10 is appreciated to continue to fund the series. Registrations are recommended but there are always a few seats available just before the start of the concert. 

 
Many thanks to our Series Patrons.

title: Learn How to Get Published with the Book Doctors
description:
As part of its ongoing writers’ workshop series, Watchung Booksellers hosts authors Arielle Eckstut and David Henry Sterry, aka The Book Doctors, to share insights on how to get published. The workshop will be held on Sunday, April 12 from 6-8:30 p.m. 
This workshop will take you through the four primary paths to publication, choosing the right idea, crafting an attention-getting pitch and query, and finding the right agent/publisher. You’ll be armed with knowledge before pitching your idea at Pitch-a-palooza during the Montclair Lit Fest! 
David Henry Sterry & Arielle Eckstut are co-founders of the Book Doctors. They are co-authors of The Essential Guide to Getting Your Book Published: How To Write It, Sell It, and Market It… Successfully. Tickets are $80 for the class and can be purchased at watchungbooksellers.com/events/writers-workshops

description:

Think of Gotta Sing as the opposite of karaoke: no one is handed a mic to sing all alone—we display the lyrics to the entire room and everyone sings together. And, unlike most karaoke, we don’t use canned, knockoff accompaniment—we play the best-known recordings, and our guests sing along with the original artists! title: Memory Café - A Dementia-Friendly Social Gathering
description:
For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.


A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.

The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.

The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.

This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.

Attendance is free but registration is required. Questions? Call 973-744-3278.

To stay informed, sign up for one or all of our eNewsletters, click here.

Photographs may be taken during our programs and events for promotional purposes such as social media and e-newsletters. If you do not wish to have your photograph taken please let us know before the event.
source: Montclair Local News, Montclair Public Library

description:

Registration is available on Handshake: https://app.joinhandshake.com/career_fairs/37dfb726-9582-4e23-9c82-6561adbc3e11/student_preview
 
Description:
Calling all community and service-minded students exploring clinical and non-clinical career options!
 
Are you looking for a job or internship? Are you curious about the career paths you can pursue with your major or graduate program? If so, the Community and Social Services Career Expo is an amazing opportunity to meet employers that align with your professional interests. Whether you are a freshman or a graduate student, this event is designed to help you explore career possibilities, gain networking experience by talking with employers, and make connections that may eventually lead to a job or internship. There will be fun mixed in with the opportunity to win raffle prizes! 
 
More Information:- Mark your calendar! Monday, April 13, 3:30pm - 6:30pm, University Hall Conference Center (7th Floor)- Visit with non-profit, government, and corporate employers that have a service-oriented mission- Discover opportunities with campus organizations and departments, including international experiences that incorporate social impact- Pre-registration is strongly encouraged - Register on Handshake!- Event details and employer list can be found on Handshake. - Dress neatly and bring resumes! Check out Rocky's Closet for free professional attire. 
 
This event is ideal for graduate and undergraduate students seeking jobs and internships in: Counseling, Child Advocacy, Justice Studies, Social Work, Political Science, Psychology and so much more!
 
Co-sponsored by: College of Humanities and Social Sciences, College for Community Health, Office of Community Engagement and Partnerships, Office of Experiential Education and Career Connections, Office of Government Relations, Office of International Academic Initiatives
 
Questions? Contact Jennifer Dudeck-Lenis at dudecklenisj@montclair.edu.

location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
A meditation in fiction on love, trauma, chance, and the nature of wild things--perfect for Earth Day. A Ghanaian psychiatrist and an American biologist who studies urban foxes bump into each other on Waterloo Bridge in London and their fates entwine when they get involved in a search for a missing boy. By a Scottish and Sierra Leonean writer whose books have been translated into 22 languages.  

“An exquisite novel about how chance and love connect us.”—The Washington Post

Aminatta Forna is a Scottish and Sierra Leonean writer whose books have been translated into 22 languages. She spent periods of her childhood in Iran, Thailand and Zambia. She is also the author of three other novels, including "The Memory of Love" as well as two works of non-fiction. She is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature

title: Midday MeetUp - Jews and Baseball, A Love Affair
description:
**Midday MeetUp - Jews and Baseball, A Love Affair**  
  
A monthly gathering to make connections and learn together.  
11:45am Catered Lunch (free)  
12:30pm Featured Program   
  
Join baseball historian Sam Bernstein for a lively survey of Jewish involvement in America’s National Pastime.  
  
Cost:** FREE or Suggested Donation of $10 per person to offset costs. (Bill My Account is only open to Shomrei Members)  
  
**RSVP:** Required so we know how much food to buy.  
https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6967e303368f110026c0c410  
  
**\***Members & PreSchool Families should use their fob to access the building.  
  
**About the Program**  
Using audio and video, *Jews and Baseball* explores the origins of the game and the impact Jewish players, owners, and innovators have had on its evolution. The program highlights figures such as Hank Greenberg, Sandy Koufax, Barney Dreyfuss, Bud Selig, Lou Boudreau, Marvin Miller, as well as the game's current Jewish stars. It also delves into topics including antisemitism in the sport, baseball’s growth in Israel, and the lore of the “Koufax Curse.”  
  
**About Sam Bernstein**  
Sam Bernstein is a retired Social Worker who has published many articles on baseball history. He received a BA in History from the American University and an MSW from Adelphi University. After a career serving the Jewish community at JCCs and Jewish Family Service, Sam worked for the Elizabeth Public Schools and as an Instructor in Social Work for Rutgers University. He was raised in Malverne, NY and moved to New Jersey with his wife Maureen in 1999.  
  
Full_Season_Schedule_for_Midday_MeetUps: https://shomrei.org/calendar/midday-meetup-calendar  
  
**Questions?** Contact June Zimmerman,   
VP for Programming  
jzimmerman@shomrei.org

Van Vleck House is pleased to present AWAKENING FROM GRIEF: Finding the Way Back to Joy – one of our most popular workshops. Led by John E. Welshons, and based on his critically acclaimed book of the same title, AWAKENING FROM GRIEF offers the opportunity to explore – and heal – the psychological, emotional and spiritual challenges that follow in the wake of a loss or unexpected change. title: She Leads with Purpose: A Women’s Leadership Workshop with Nicole & Lauren
description:
Great leadership today requires more than performance. It requires clarity, authenticity, and the courage to lead in alignment with who you truly are. 
This Women’s History Month, join a dynamic community of corporate leaders, founders, entrepreneurs, and women in management roles who are committed to leading with purpose. 
We’ll begin with a quick well-being check-in to measure where you are showing up at your strongest and where greater alignment may unlock more energy, impact, and fulfillment in your leadership. 
From there, we’ll explore how women can lead more powerfully by leveraging their unique strengths, values, and voice and by defining success on their own terms. 
This workshop brings together accomplished women who are committed to leading with intention, expanding their influence, and supporting one another’s growth.

location: Alexander Kasser Theater, Montclair State University, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
A highly inventive new musical by César Alvarez and Emily Orling, The Elementary Spacetime Show tells the story of Alameda: a young girl who enters a liminal void somewhere in between life and death. Alameda must pass through the eight existential trials of a cosmic Vaudevillian game show to discover the possibility that her darkness is a gift. Her journey is set to a kaleidoscopic contemporary score that bravely handles the subject of teenage suicide with both sensitivity and vibrant showmanship, blending sly humor with emotional nuance.

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support!
All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program.
Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair.

Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least $20.26 and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe. 
For a gift of $40, celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord.

How do I get my customized philanthropy cord?
Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up:

Tuesday, October 28 from 1:00 – 3:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Thursday, November 20  from 1:00 – 3:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Tuesday, December 2 from 12:00 – 3:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Bloomfield Campus Graduation Fair: Wednesday, December 10th from 12:00 – 6:00 p.m. in Deacon’s Den, Talbott Hall (for Bloomfield graduates only)
Montclair Campus Graduation Fairs: Thursday, December 11th from 10:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m. in the Student Center Ballrooms (for Montclair or Bloomfield graduates)

Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. The last day we will mail the cords is Monday, December 22, 2025 at 2:30 p.m. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement.
Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward!For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.

title: The DJ Academy: Music Matters 101
description:
DJing is one of the original elements of Hip Hop and is often considered the first. Hip Hop began in the Bronx during the 1970s at community block parties, where DJs used turntables to bring people together through music. Early pioneers like DJ Kool Herc introduced breakbeats by looping the most rhythmic parts of records, creating the foundation for breaking and shaping how dancers and MCs interacted with the music.
As Hip Hop evolved, DJing became the musical backbone of the culture. DJs provide the beats for MCing, set the tempo for dancers, and control the energy of Hip Hop spaces by reading the crowd and responding in real time. Through techniques like scratching, cutting, and beat juggling, DJs helped define Hip Hop’s sound while preserving its history and passing down cultural knowledge.
This class introduces the basics of DJing and how music shapes the dance experience. DJ Bascis will explain core concepts such as tempo, rhythm, and song structure, helping students understand how music guides movement and energy on the dance floor.
Participants will learn how DJs choose music, create smooth transitions, and adjust the vibe based on the room. 
Through simple examples and live demonstrations, students will build confidence in listening to music with intention. This can bewhether they are dancing, freestyling, or interested in DJing themselves.
This class is designed for beginners and college students, with no prior DJ or music experience required.

Hosted by: Campus Activities at Bloomfield

title: Protecting Your Financial Future: FINRA Investor Advocacy Program
description:
Want to protect your financial future? This presentation is designed to help individuals guard against financial fraud and to make informed decisions before entrusting your money with financial professionals. Participants will leave with a basic understanding of how to spot red flags, an overview of investor rights, and insight into what the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority ("FINRA") is and how it can help investors when problems arise. 

Andrew Marino is a 2026 J.D. Candidate at Seton Hall University School of Law and a Student Advocate for the FINRA Investor Advocacy Program (“IAP”). He is a life-long resident of New Jersey and graduated from Denison University. Mr. Marino has worked as a judicial intern for the District Court of New Jersey, as well as a Summer Associate for a New Jersey firm. Mr. Marino also serves as a Senior Editor for the Seton Hall Law Review. 

 This free, 45-minute presentation is for educational purposes and does not sell or recommend any financial services. The FINRA IAP is one of 10 securities arbitration clinics throughout the United States. The FINRA IAP program at Seton Hall is a pro bono program, which provides free legal representation to New Jersey residents of modest means with securities fraud claims. The IAP was established by a grant from FINRA.

location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Yom HahShoah Program: After the Holocaust: Family History, Memory, and Identity
description:
**Community Program:**   
7:15PM: Light Meal  
7:40PM - 9:00PM: Program  
  
**After the Holocaust:** **Family History, Memory, and Identity**  
In the aftermath of World War II, Jewish survivors in Displaced Persons (DP) camps rebuilt their lives with remarkable resilience, creating families and ushering in an unprecedented baby boom. At the same time, family memory—preserved through stories, documents, and traditions—became a powerful means of reconstructing identity after profound loss. In this lecture, Dr. Serafima Velkovich explores how family history research and personal narratives intersect with the history of DP camps and demonstrates how individuals can uncover traces of former DP babies within their own family histories.  
  
*Join a conversation with Dr. Sera Velkovich of Yad Vashem and Shirley Grill of Shomrei Emunah as they explore the resilience, and rebuilding of lives in the aftermath of the Shoah.*

location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Nothing says The Twilight Zone like stories about enchanted objects, mystical forces or the presence of magic. Though they are interesting elements in the stories, the real intrigue lies with how the episodes’ characters behave in their presence. Driven by desperation, curiosity or just plain fear, we get the opportunity to witness lessons learned whether the result is salvation or human downfall.


During five episodes, we will see various responses to the unexplained. Whether they are controlled by superstition, are mishandling seemingly ordinary objects or dismissing what is not fully understood, each character must face the life-changing consequences
of their decisions.


Please join Linda Hetcher this season in the interactive study of the supernatural, most notably presented in The Twilight Zone.

title: A Night of Jazz with the Bradford Hayes Quartet
description:
The Bradford Hayes Quartet featuring Bradford Hayes on Saxophone, Michael Cochrane on Piano, Takashi Otsuka on Bass and Gordon Lane on Drums will perform a set of originals and classic jazz hits. 

About the Artist
Bradford Hayes, a native of Dinwiddie County, Virginia has been a force on the jazz scene for many years now. He has performed at a number of clubs, colleges and concert halls that include Birdland (NYC), L'Entrepot (Paris, FRANCE) and the Beacon Theater (NYC). Bradford has performed in different musical settings with Jimmy Heath, Al Grey, Cecil Payne, Rufus Reid, Ray Bryant, Ted Curson, Charles Davis, Joe Lee Wilson, Ben Riley, Dr. Lonnie Smith, Cecil Brooks III, Steve Colson, Kelvin Bell, Pheeroan Aklaff, Michael Cochrane, James Weidman, Nabaté Isles and Donald Braden. Mr. Hayes’ band has also shared the stage with the bands of Gerald Albright, Chico Freeman, Betty Carter, Joe Henderson, Max Roach, Marlena Shaw, Pieces of a Dream, and Hilton Ruiz among others. In addition to leading his own band, Bradford worked with Babatunde Olatunji’s Drums of Passion Band for 15 years until Mr. Olatunji’s passing. Bradford, along with Javon Jackson, Hilton Ruiz, John Lee, and Bill Saxton, was photographed by legendary jazz photographer William Gottlieb in what sadly turned out to be the last jazz photo taken by Mr. Gottlieb. This was the first photo of musicians taken by Mr. Gottlieb since 1948. In addition to this photo session Bradford and the other musicians selected, are also featured as part of a soon to be aired PBS documentary about Mr. Gottlieb. Bradford recently performed a series of concerts in collaboration with the New Jersey Symphony Orchestra as well as a performance with Avant Garde Pianist Steve “Adegoke” Colson at the New Jersey Performing Arts Center.

Mr. Hayes holds a Bachelor of Sciences Degree in Music Education from North Carolina A&T State University in Greensboro, North Carolina. He also studied privately with George Coleman and Charles Davis.

www.bradfordhayes.com

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: Where Do We Go From Here: Chaos or Community? Film event and discussion 7:30 at FCC
description:
Join us in a conversation for our time. Foremost Productions will present “A Community Cultural Event Honoring the Legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and Dr. Maya Angelou” at the First Congregational Church of Montclair. 

The evening will feature a screening of the award-winning documentary film “Maya Angelou – Reflections of a Blessed Soul,” followed by a special talkback discussion to include the film’s director Hafiz Farid and executive producer Shelley Grodner Seidenstein.

Inspired by Dr. King’s timeless question, “Where Do We Go From Here: Chaos or Community?”, the evening invites audiences to explore the relevance of the words and wisdom of both Dr.King and Dr. Angelou in today’s world. 

The event is free and open to the public, made possible through the support of community sponsors who believe in the importance of accessible cultural programming.

“We can learn to see each other and see ourselves in each other and recognize that human beings are more alike than we are unalike.” -Maya Angelou

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist project.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Passaic Watershed Mountain and Valley Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for a very happy loop hike, more in our Passaic River series, but this time filling in some gaps of interesting places we missed on previous trips, and featuring Garrett Mountain and Rifle Camp Park this time!
We will meet at 9 am at West Falls Plaza, which we've used a couple of times, and make our way to the Passaic River. This time, we'll cross the river and follow a road upstream on the opposite side we did last time.
We'll get off of the road and walk through Laurel Grove and Mt Nebo Cemeteries, and then Holy Sepulchre Cemetery after a few blocks of road walk.
We will then take the West Side Park trails and Riverside Terrace to the east for a bit. This will lead us around the Great Falls again covering a couple of different trails from before. We then come up past the Reservoir, cross Rt 80 at New Street, and head up into Garrett Mountain Park. We'll make our way through there, and loop in a roundabout way through that park south to Rifle Camp Park. We'll loop from the east side of that as far south as we can, then back to the north on the west side. This will then take us back to Garrett Mountain, and we'll descend west though Zekeriah Park.
A few blocks on the road takes us through Diane Grimes Park, then a bit more to the Morris Canal Greenway. We will loop back to where we started from here to close this very diverse 15 mile loop.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Savory and Sweet Arab Cuisine: Fattoush Salad and Jallab NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.



In another edition of FARAH’s Sweet & Savory Flavors of Arab Cuisine series at MPL, discover the aromatic spices of Arab cuisine. Join Lilianne Gooch for a guided cooking demonstration on how to make two classic dishes with an emphasis on spices: one sweet and one savory. 
 



Fattoush: The Vibrant Taste of the Levant

The perfect chopped salad, Fattoush is a refreshing, crunchy, and colorful staple in Arab cuisine featuring watercress or romaine lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, and fresh herbs, all tossed in a tangy signature lemon-sumac-pomegranate molasses vinaigrette. Added crunch and flavor comes from crispy toasted pita chips topped with za’atar. Join us to learn about the unique spices that make up this flavorful Arab salad.  
 



Jallab: The Essence of Arab Hospitality

Transport your senses to the Levant with this traditional and refreshing drink. Learn how to mix date, grape and carob molasses with rose water into a fragrant non-alcoholic drink. Perfect for warm days, it is traditionally served chilled and topped with pine nuts and raisins. This is the quintessential Arab mocktail.

title: Creating a Compelling College Application (High School Juniors & Families)
description:
This is an online presentation; you must sign up here to gain access.
From our friends at Stand Out for College:

We are offering this Zoom presentation to help high school juniors and their parents understand how to use the upcoming summer productively to create a compelling college application.

We will cover the college application process, including current admissions trends, writing the personal statement and supplemental essays, securing strong teacher recommendations, and understanding how students can position themselves to increase their chances of admission.

We will also explore why a student’s ability to express insights, experiences, and personal growth through their essays is more important than ever.

Our presentation will include application strategies, such as the advantages and disadvantages of early decision, early action, and regular decision. We will review the factors students should consider when deciding whether to submit standardized test scores for test optional colleges and universities. We will also explain the different pathways through which students can be admitted to a particular school.

We will examine the holistic admissions review process, what admissions officers consider important when evaluating applicants, and how students can develop a compelling narrative that strengthens their applications.

We will also discuss the importance of community service and how it offers opportunities for personal growth and character development. Admissions officers place significant emphasis on a student’s character and the ways they have contributed to their communities.

This program provides a detailed and strategic overview of what students should focus on to make their college applications as compelling as possible.

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: Parent Academy Series School Year 2025-2026
description:
The Parent Academy is an engaging monthly program that runs September through June where parents and caregivers can learn practical tools and strategies to support their youth’s mental well-being. Each session focuses on a specific mental health topic and provides helpful resources and tips that can be used right away. 
These sessions are psychoeducational webinars, not to be used in place of clinical treatment. 
TOPICS: 
Suicide Prevention – Wednesday 9/17 12-1:00pm
Developed by the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, the session is designed to help parents, teachers, and other caring adults recognize the warning signs of suicide in youth, initiate conversations around depression and suicidal thoughts, and guide them in helping young people access needed support and resources.  
Teen Dating Violence: Visible & Voiced – Tuesday 10/21 6:30-7:30pm
This session equips parents with the tools to recognize signs of dating violence in teens and respond with confidence. Learn how to spot red flags, support open communication, and help your teen build safe, healthy relationships.  
Less Stress, More Joy: Holiday Prep for Parents – Wednesday 11/12 12-1:00pm
This interactive webinar will help you plan for a more peaceful and meaningful holiday season. NJ4S will share simple strategies and practical tools to help you set healthy boundaries, manage stress, and prioritize your well-being.  
Spotting the Signs: A Guide to Youth Substance Use Awareness – Tuesday 12/9 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY Center for Prevention and Counseling
Participants will be equipped with tools and knowledge to recognize and respond to youth substance use.  
Suicide & Social Media – Wednesday 1/21 6:30-8:00pm
PRESENTED BY Jonathan Singer Ph.D., LCSW
This webinar will translate the most important research on social media and suicide risk into practical tips.  
Eating Disorders 101 – Tuesday 2/24 6:30-7:30pm
Information, signs to recognize, and resources will be shared on the topics of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge-eating disorders.  
High Stakes: The Rising Risk of Youth Gambling – Tuesday 3/10 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY New Bridge Services Information will be shared about the growing issue of youth gambling, shedding light on trends, what to look for, and available resources.  
Parent/Caregiver Support for Children on the Spectrum – Tuesday 4/21 6:30-7:30pm 
The session will provide a safe, supportive, and empowering space for parents/caregivers of children on the autism spectrum to connect, share topics, and build resilience through tools for mental health, self-care, and caregiving.  
A Parent’s Guide to Youth Mental Health – Wednesday 5/13 6:30-7:30pm
This webinar will focus on the various aspects of mental health, how to have the conversation with a youth in your life, and what to expect after the conversation.  
Bored to Brave: Building Independence through Community Adventures this Summer – Tuesday 6/2 12-1:00pm
This webinar will cover the impact of changing schedules, empowering youth to reduce screen time, and creating opportunities within the home, neighborhood, and community. Our NJ4S summer programs will be noted, as well as free resources within the counties.

title: The DJ Academy: Music Matters 101
description:
DJing is one of the original elements of Hip Hop and is often considered the first. Hip Hop began in the Bronx during the 1970s at community block parties, where DJs used turntables to bring people together through music. Early pioneers like DJ Kool Herc introduced breakbeats by looping the most rhythmic parts of records, creating the foundation for breaking and shaping how dancers and MCs interacted with the music.
As Hip Hop evolved, DJing became the musical backbone of the culture. DJs provide the beats for MCing, set the tempo for dancers, and control the energy of Hip Hop spaces by reading the crowd and responding in real time. Through techniques like scratching, cutting, and beat juggling, DJs helped define Hip Hop’s sound while preserving its history and passing down cultural knowledge.
This class introduces the basics of DJing and how music shapes the dance experience. DJ Bascis will explain core concepts such as tempo, rhythm, and song structure, helping students understand how music guides movement and energy on the dance floor.
Participants will learn how DJs choose music, create smooth transitions, and adjust the vibe based on the room. 
Through simple examples and live demonstrations, students will build confidence in listening to music with intention. This can bewhether they are dancing, freestyling, or interested in DJing themselves.
This class is designed for beginners and college students, with no prior DJ or music experience required.

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world!

title: Why Godzilla Still Matters: Montclair State Professor Jason Abbott to Speak in Brooklyn
description:
Why Godzilla Still Matters: Montclair State Professor Jason Abbott to Speak in Brooklyn
Dr. Jason Abbott, Professor of Political Science and International Relations at Montclair State University, will deliver a public lecture as part of the Lectures on Tap series in Brooklyn, New York.
 
Title: Godzilla: Japan, Trauma, and the Unkillable MonsterDate: Wednesday, April 22, 2026Time: 6:30 p.m. – 8:30 p.m. (Lecture begins at 7:00 p.m.)Location: Bushwick, Brooklyn, NY (exact address provided upon registration)Please Register: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/lectures-on-tap-godzilla-japan-trauma-and-the-unkillable-monster-tickets-1985135400421?aff=oddtdtcreator
 
Lectures on Tap is a public lecture series that brings professors, experts, and storytellers into informal venues to deliver accessible, thought-provoking talks.
 
In this lecture, Dr. Abbott examines Godzilla as a cultural lens through which to understand Japan’s postwar experience. Emerging in the shadow of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Godzilla has long served as a cinematic reflection of national trauma, nuclear anxiety, and unresolved historical memory. The talk explores why the figure of Godzilla reappears at moments of crisis and what this enduring monster reveals about how societies process catastrophe and construct collective memory.
 
Drawing on examples across multiple films and historical periods, the lecture considers how trauma is not simply resolved, but often reworked and reimagined over time.
Agenda:6:30 p.m. – Doors open; seating, food, and drinks available6:55 p.m. – Host introduction7:00 p.m. – Lecture begins7:45 p.m. – Audience Q&A8:00 p.m. – Informal discussion and networking8:30 p.m. – Event concludes

title: Movie screening: "The Little Things That Run the World" - Earth Week Celebration
location: Guild Room at First Congregational Church, 40 South Fullerton Avenue, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042, 07042, United States
description:
Join us for a screening of “The Little Things That Run the World,” part of our Bee City USA program. 
Synopsis:
Life on Earth is in the middle of a major re-alignment of species composition. The smallest of creatures – insects – hold the fabric of all life together. They are the most numerous of all animal groups on the planet. But insects are declining at an alarming rate throughout the world, threatening innumerable species, whole ecosystems, and even our food systems with collapse. This is story about untangling the mysteries as to why something so ubiquitous – and seemingly endless – could be on the cusp of disappearing entirely. It is also the story of heroic efforts to save these most vulnerable of creatures. 
Admission is free. Register to save your seat. 
Learn more about the film here. 
*The movie will begin promptly at 7 pm; please arrive by 6:45.

description:

title: African Dance for Beginners NEW
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.


	
		
			
			Join us for our all-new African Dance Workshop, an exciting opportunity to move, connect, and celebrate culture through rhythm and community. Led by Karen Miles of Zawadi African Dance and accompanied by two live drummers, this energizing class welcomes dancers of all levels.
			
		
	


The workshop begins with a 10-minute guided warm-up to prepare the body with rhythmic movement and grounding techniques. Participants will then learn Dansa, a vibrant traditional dance of the Malinké people from Upper Guinea.

Dansa is traditionally performed as a joyful celebration during community gatherings, often encouraging collective labor while strengthening unity and fostering a powerful spirit of togetherness. Experience the rich cultural traditions, dynamic rhythms, and uplifting communal energy that make West African dance so inspiring.

Note: This class takes place at DiRasa Gallery, 4 Lackawanna Plaza in Montclair.

title: Open Book, Open Mind; Michael Luo, "Strangers in the Land"
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
New Yorker writer and executive editor Michael Luo will talk to Matthew Purdy, editor at large of The New York Times, about about his landmark study, "Strangers in the Land: Exclusion, Belonging, and the Epic Story of the Chinese in America." Co-presented by AAPI New Jersey.

“You can’t paint a complete picture of America without [the story of Chinese Americans], and the New Yorker journalist Michael Luo tells it persuasively in 'Strangers in the Land'... [The book] succeeds through its little biographies of individuals – a range of quirky and fascinating figures, both Chinese and white, who drive the narrative. . . [and offer] a view on the full complexity of American immigration.” —The New York Times Book Review



Doors open at 6 p.m. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book sales and signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: Casual Volleyball - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
We're a group of people who will start by hitting the ball around for the first 20-30 minutes and then we'll break up into 2-4 teams for two or three hours of play.

If we have more than 20 people show up, we'll break up into three or four teams of 6 (Some may have 7, 8 or 9. Additional players just rotate into play). Games will be to 10 points. Rally scoring. Winner stays on (unless a team has won four straight).

We'll be heading outdoors to the hard court in Leonia off Overpeck County Pk Driveway in the Overpeck County Park.

\*\*\* After playing, we'll be likely heading to Tropical Juice Bar, an idea of regular attendee Kate, for a drink and snack. It's located at 60 River St. in Hackensack. Feel free to join us or suggest another spot for a post-volleyball hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play volleyball and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. We're more for people who haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play again and hang out.

Directions: You can Google "Volleyball Court in Leonia" and it should come up. Or type 41 Willow Tree Road, Leonia, NJ 07605 into your GPS, but note that it's not on Willow Tree Road, just near it. Instead, turn onto Overpeck County Pk Driveway off Fort Lee Road (Degraw Avenue). It is past the tennis courts and near a basketball court and track. You can try Googling Leonia High School as well. That should help you find it.

We don't have the court reserved and if it happens to be taken, we may play with those already occupying it or we will try to relocate on the fly. It's certainly possible that we may have to cancel that day if we can't find a suitable spot. Please keep that in mind. And if it's looking like it'll rain or snow, I'll make a call on whether to cancel around an hour ahead of time.

Please bring a ball and net if you have them for possible use during the game. Feel free to bring a speaker for music, or snacks and drinks for consumption during play.

If you have trouble finding the court or group, you can call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609. There is plenty of parking and an open bathroom at the park.

Hope you'll join us for our 18th volleyball event. Questions or comments? You can message Andy on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609.

Check out bowling, soccer, volleyball, tennis or one of our other activities at: www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Hike w/ Kirk of RRWA! 3-4 mi
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Sunday, April 26. 3 - 5:30pm

Use this link to register: https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation. Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the
Rahway River up South Mountain. **Focus on ecology and hydrology**, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues.

Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs.

Sponsered by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association.

Meet at Clipper Pavilion in South Mountain

Reservation on Cherry Lane in West Orange. Advance registration required via Rahway River Watershed. Use this link to register: https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html

Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. Reception immediately following  
  
RSVP: http://shomrei.org/hurwitz  
  
**About the Program**  
Award-winning author Sarah Hurwitz joins Rabbi Julie Roth for a candid conversation about rediscovering Judaism as an adult and why its intellectual depth and moral clarity feel strikingly relevant to modern life. From finding meaning in a chaotic world to standing tall against rising antisemitism, Sarah explores why embracing Jewish wisdom isn’t just about honoring the past -- it’s about sanctifying the present and elevating our shared humanity.   
  
**Free Babysitting Available**  
Email Aviva Arad, aarad@shomrei.org  
  
**\*Additional parking is available next door at 73 & 77 Park Street.**  
  
**In Loving Memory of Seth Goodchild**   
Seth Goodchild was inspired by his family to convert to Judaism at the end of his life. To honor his legacy and share his love of Judaism, his friends and family sponsored this lecture and a class on exploring Judaism.

After years of playing in casual Mah Jongg games, more experienced players may be looking to challenge themselves in tournament play but feel intimidated by the idea.  Are you good enough? title: (POSTPONED) LIVING GREEN: Change Your Diet, Help the Planet NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School class. Click below to register.

The food we eat-- how it is produced, processed, and shipped--has a huge environmental impact, and is a significant driver of climate change. Project Drawdown, a leading nonprofit research hub that identifies, reviews, and promotes the most effective, science-based solutions to reverse global warming, found that decreasing our consumption of animal products is one of the most important things that people can do to help slow climate change and improve the natural environment on our planet. Come to this session to learn more about how our food system affects the environment, and how can you start moving towards a greener--and healthier--diet.

Students will speak using the present tense and will be introduced to simple grammar to express past time.  We will review many relevant expressions and vocabulary in context. This course will be appropriate for students who have completed Italian for Travelers 1 and 2 or Basic Italian 1 & 2.

title: Denim Day 2026: Mind the Gaps, Move Forward
description:
April is Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and together, we can break the silence. The Montclair State University Police Department and the Office of Advocacy & Outreach are committed to fostering a campus where survivors feel heard, supported, and empowered. It starts with believing. It starts with you. By offering a safe and affirming response to those who disclose gender-based and sexual violence, we can create lasting change. Let’s stand together to end the cycle of silence—because every voice matters, and every action counts.
Denim Day is recognized internationally as a day of action and awareness, encouraging people to wear denim to challenge victim-blaming and educate others about sexual violence. This year, Denim Day falls on Wednesday, April 29, 2026.
The University Police and Office of Advocacy & Outreach and the Office of Advocacy and Community Resilience, in partnership with over 30 campus and local community organizations, invites you to join us from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at the Amphitheater for a powerful awareness event honoring survivors and increasing awareness of available resources.
Despite the gaps that still exist in the criminal justice system, in resources, and in prevention education, we will move forward together as a community. As part of this commitment, we will walk one mile around campus in solidarity with survivors.

Hosted by: Advocacy and Outreach

description:

Each meeting highlights a theme related to science education, from classroom strategies to career pathways, and offers students opportunities to connect with mentors, explore internships, and gain real-world experience working with teachers and children. Students are encouraged to bring a guest who may also be interested in exploring science teaching.
These gatherings help us build a strong community of support, where students encourage one another, share experiences, and access valuable opportunities such as scholarships, paid internships, and mentoring from advanced peers and in-service science teachers. Whether you are just beginning to explore the idea of teaching or already on the path toward certification, these meetings are a place to grow, learn, and belong.

Hosted by: College of Science and Mathematics (CSAM)

title: Celebration of Life Service for Adriana O'Toole
Bowling Night - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to Davey's Irish Pub & Restaurant, 5 Park St. in Montvale, or The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** First, find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 23rd bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, ping pong, skating or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Hike w/ Kirk of RRWA! 3-4 mi
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Saturday, May 9, 10am - 12:30 pm

Click to register: https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation
Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the
Rahway River up South Mountain.

Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway
Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues.

Good balance required. Children welcome.
No dogs. Sponsered by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association. Meet at Clipper Pavilion in South
Mountain Reservation on Cherry Lane in West Orange. Advance registration required via rahwayriver.org/calendar.html . Email
president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

\*\*\* In registering for this or any other South Mountain Conservancy (SMC) programs in 2026 online, I hereby release and agree to hold the SMC, its volunteers, staff and Board of Trustees, harmless from and waive on behalf of myself, my heirs, and any personal representatives any and all causes of action, claims, demands, damages, costs, expenses and compensation for damage or loss to myself and/or property that may be caused by any act, or failure to act, in this SMC activity, or that may otherwise arise in any way in connection with any other SMC activity. I understand that this release discharges the SMC from any liability or claim that I, my heirs, or any personal representatives, may have against the SMC with respect to any bodily injury, illness, death, medical treatment, or property damage that may arise from, or in connection to, any SMC program. This liability waiver and release extends to the SMC along with Essex County and its staff and any other affiliated organization or SMC partner. I also understand that by signing below I approve the possible use of photos of me at this SMC event on social media or in promotional materials.
**BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**
**Am following all CDC recommended guidelines, above, and limiting my exposure to the novel coronavirus/COVID-19.**
\# Arrival\, Weather\, & Cancellations
Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. Wear hiking boots, preferably waterproof with good soles and traction devices and bring poles (optional).** Dogs are not allowed on hikes unless specified.
These hikes are publicized first to SMC members and then advertised to the public one week before a hike. There is a limit of 25 participants, so pre-registration is required at least two days before a hike to sign the liability waiver online and allow lists to be sent to hike leaders. If you have registered and then find you cannot attend, please cancel your order online. **Repeated no shows without prior cancellation will result in removal from list.**

description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

title: Forest Therapy Gentle Walk w/ JoJo ~1mi
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
A gentle, grounding Forest Therapy experience designed to help you slow down, connect with nature, and restore your senses. We will remain within a mile of our starting point at Tulip Springs, moving only short distances as needed for comfort and exploration.

This is not a long-distance hike, the focus is presence, noticing, and guided invitations that support relaxation and calm.

Welcome to bring something to sit on and a journal.

Due to the nature of this walk, no kids nor dogs. Just let me know if you'd like a family walk and we can schedule.

Meet at: Tulip Springs in the parking lot across the bridge

**Arrival: Please arrive 15 minutes before the start time for check‑in and settling in.**

Leader: Jojo Abenaavi Wright, cell # 973‑592-9062

\*\*\* In registering for this or any other South Mountain Conservancy (SMC) programs in 2026 online, I hereby release and agree to hold the SMC, its volunteers, staff and Board of Trustees, harmless from and waive on behalf of myself, my heirs, and any personal representatives any and all causes of action, claims, demands, damages, costs, expenses and compensation for damage or loss to myself and/or property that may be caused by any act, or failure to act, in this SMC activity, or that may otherwise arise in any way in connection with any other SMC activity. I understand that this release discharges the SMC from any liability or claim that I, my heirs, or any personal representatives, may have against the SMC with respect to any bodily injury, illness, death, medical treatment, or property damage that may arise from, or in connection to, any SMC program. This liability waiver and release extends to the SMC along with Essex County and its staff and any other affiliated organization or SMC partner. I also understand that by signing below I approve the possible use of photos of me at this SMC event on social media or in promotional materials.
**BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**
**Am following all CDC recommended guidelines, above, and limiting my exposure to the novel coronavirus/COVID-19.**
\# Arrival\, Weather\, & Cancellations
Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. Wear hiking boots, preferably waterproof with good soles and traction devices and bring poles (optional).** Dogs are not allowed on hikes unless specified.
These hikes are publicized first to SMC members and then advertised to the public one week before a hike. There is a limit of 25 participants, so pre-registration is required at least two days before a hike to sign the liability waiver online and allow lists to be sent to hike leaders. If you have registered and then find you cannot attend, please cancel your order online. **Repeated no shows without prior cancellation will result in removal from list.**

title: Midday MeetUp - Bonnie Rapp, Best of Broadway
description:
**Midday MeetUp - Bonnie Rapp, Best of Broadway   
A monthly gathering to make connections and learn together.  
11:45am Catered Lunch (free)  
12:30pm Featured Program   
  
Experience *The Best of Broadway* as Bonnie Rapp brings to life unforgettable moments from Tony Award–winning musicals. Relive the golden age of musical theatre through beloved classics and timeless melodies by legendary composers such as Rodgers and Hammerstein, Lerner and Loewe, Frank Loesser, Irving Berlin and more!  
  
Cost:** FREE or Suggested Donation of $10 per person to offset costs. (Bill My Account is only open to Shomrei Members)  
  
**RSVP:** Required so we know how much food to buy.  
https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6967e6f2368f110026c0c486  
  
**\***Members & PreSchool Families should use their fob to access the building.  
 About Bonnie Rapp**  
Bonnie had the honor of performing the lead role of Christine Daaé in the National Tour/San Francisco Company of Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera. Some of Bonnie’s favorite roles include Maria in The Sound of Music, Kate in Kiss Me, Kate, Cinderella in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella, Louise in Gypsy and Sister Amnesia and Sister Leo in Nunsense, Nunsense II and Nunsense Jamboree. In addition, Bonnie has appeared in numerous galas, fundraisers, and Broadway concerts, including performances at Lincoln Center's Avery Fisher Hall.  
  
For the past decade, Bonnie has devoted her talents to providing live musical entertainment for a wide range of audiences, including corporate and community events, libraries, private celebrations, JCCs, and residents of independent living, assisted living, nursing homes, and memory care communities.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.
